# UniverLab

> UniverLab is an independent computational laboratory that turns real needs into open experiments — developer tools, scientific workflows, and agent systems. Every experiment ships open knowledge: tools, libraries, datasets, and papers. Founded by Jheison Martinez Bolivar. The site is bilingual (English and Spanish).

Different problems, one method: take work that lives in fragile, manual procedures and make it explicit, reproducible and automatable — by a person or by an agent. UniverLab follows one loop: a real need becomes an open experiment, and that experiment gives back open knowledge — the experiment is the work, and everything it ships is a byproduct. The lab is guided by a philosophy it calls Pensamiento Cósmico: technology as the medium through which curiosity becomes reality, software meant to outlive trends, and knowledge kept open. In practice that means open-source CLIs you can install today, experiments you can reproduce, and documentation that ships with the code.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://univerlab.org/): What UniverLab is, the experiment loop, research directions, and the experiment index.
- [Manifesto — Pensamiento Cósmico](https://univerlab.org/manifesto/): The philosophy behind the lab — a philosophy of the continuity of consciousness, and the values that guide which experiments get built.
- [Contributors](https://univerlab.org/contributors/): The people and language models behind the lab, and how to contribute.
- [Experiments](https://univerlab.org/experiments/): Every experiment of the lab, each with its machine: the tools you can install today, the research in progress, and what was archived.

## Experiments

- [Harness Canopy](https://univerlab.org/canopy/): EXP-001 (active) — a graph engine for AI coding agents — every harness, one workflow — with cross-agent coordination, RAG, context transfer, mission/sync signalling, and prompt templates.
- [TexForge](https://univerlab.org/texforge/): EXP-002 (active) — a unified workspace and CLI for LaTeX that compiles documents to PDF, renders diagrams, and manages templates without installing a multi-gigabyte TeX distribution.
- [GitKit](https://univerlab.org/gitkit/): EXP-003 (active) — git tooling that wires up `.gitattributes` and git hooks automatically the moment a repository lands on disk, so every repo starts configured.
- [ghScaff](https://univerlab.org/ghscaff/): EXP-004 (active) — scaffolds a complete GitHub repository (manifests, entry points, CI/release workflows) in one step; Rust today, more languages on the way.
- [Astro Denoise](https://univerlab.org/astro-denoise/): EXP-006 (research) — a reproducible benchmarking platform for denoising methods on astronomical images (a master's thesis project).
- [DemoStage](https://univerlab.org/demostage/): EXP-007 (active) — records terminal and app demos as editable event files you can prune, pace, and replay, exporting to cast, html, or gif.
- [Quorum](https://univerlab.org/quorum/): EXP-008 (active) — serverless planning poker that runs peer-to-peer over WebRTC: share a link, estimate together, no sign-up required.

## Optional

- [GitHub organization](https://github.com/UniverLab): Source code for every experiment.
- [Archive](https://univerlab.org/archive/): Experiments that were built and discontinued, and ideas that were never built, each recorded with the reason.
- [Spanish site](https://univerlab.org/es/): The full site in Spanish.

## Live

- Logbook: https://univerlab.org/status/index.md — the latest lab entries, rendered live from the announcements API on every request.
- Roadmap: https://univerlab.org/roadmap/index.md — every roadmap item by lane (now, next, later, ideas, recently shipped), rendered live from the announcements API on every request.
- Atom feed: https://announcements.univerlab.org/feed.atom — the same logbook entries, in your reader.
- Agent catalog: https://univerlab.org/.well-known/ai-catalog.json — what an agent can use here: the API catalog, the Agent Skills index and this file.
- MCP server: https://univerlab.org/mcp — four read-only tools for agents (roadmap, logbook, about, mission dates). Server Card: https://univerlab.org/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json

- [Privacy Policy](https://univerlab.org/privacy/): What UniverLab records across its services, why, how long it lasts, and the rights you have.
- [Terms of Use](https://univerlab.org/terms/): The rules for using UniverLab sites and tools, community graphs, code licences, and Colombian law.
